title: Benefit Overpayment Accounts — Arrears Share for Claimants with Support or SNAP Obligations
content:
The installment part of the arrears payment on a defaulted Benefit Overpayment Accounts repayment plan is reduced for a claimant who carries other support or benefit-repayment obligations on the Department's withholding records, the claimant's Benefit Withholding and Deduction Orders.

## The two obligations

1. **Current child support of at least USD 75.00 a week**: an order of the kind Child Support Withholding — Current Support Order, with status active, whose weekly amount is at least the support threshold of USD 75.00.
2. **SNAP overissuance recovery**: an order of the kind SNAP Overissuance Recovery — Household or Agency Error or SNAP Overissuance Recovery — Intentional Program Violation, with status active.

## Share of the installment part paid

| Obligation 1 | Obligation 2 | Share of the installment part the claimant pays |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | 0.5, the two-obligation share (50 percent) |
| Yes | No | 0.75, the one-obligation share (75 percent) |
| No | Yes | 0.75, the one-obligation share (75 percent) |
| No | No | The installment part in full |

The installment part is the installments counted times the price of each installment, less the installment credit, never less than zero.

## Desk points

- An active Child Support Withholding — Current Support Order with a weekly amount below USD 75.00 does not count as obligation 1.
- Orders that are not active (requested, suspended, revoked or terminated) do not count.
- Only the two obligations named above count; any other claimant pays the installment part in full.
- *Hypothetical:* an installment part of USD 480.00 becomes USD 240.00 when both obligations are on the records and USD 360.00 when one is.
